commit 2ed84f55b22f19a1e1e8eea2e50963dce62052d3
Author: Ash Berlin-Taylor <ash_github@firemirror.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 7 00:55:02 2021 +0100

    Switch LGPL'd chardet for MIT licensed charset_normalizer (#5797)
    
    Although using the (non-vendored) chardet library is fine for requests
    itself, but using a LGPL dependency the story is a lot less clear
    for downstream projects, particularly ones that might like to bundle
    requests (and thus chardet) in to a single binary -- think something
    similar to what docker-compose is doing. By including an LGPL'd module
    it is no longer clear if the resulting artefact must also be LGPL'd.
    
    By changing out this dependency for one under MIT we remove all
    license ambiguity.
    
    As an "escape hatch" I have made the code so that it will use chardet
    first if it is installed, but we no longer depend upon it directly,
    although there is a new extra added, `requests[lgpl]`. This should
    minimize the impact to users, and give them an escape hatch if
    charset_normalizer turns out to be not as good. (In my non-exhaustive
    tests it detects the same encoding as chartdet in every case I threw at
    it)
    
    Co-authored-by: Jarek Potiuk <jarek@potiuk.com>
    
    Co-authored-by: Jarek Potiuk <jarek@potiuk.com>

Author: Ash Berlin-Taylor <ash_github@firemirror.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 7 00:55:02 2021 +0100

    Switch LGPL'd chardet for MIT licensed charset_normalizer (#5797)
    
    Although using the (non-vendored) chardet library is fine for requests
    itself, but using a LGPL dependency the story is a lot less clear
    for downstream projects, particularly ones that might like to bundle
    requests (and thus chardet) in to a single binary -- think something
    similar to what docker-compose is doing. By including an LGPL'd module
    it is no longer clear if the resulting artefact must also be LGPL'd.
    
    By changing out this dependency for one under MIT we remove all
    license ambiguity.
    
    As an "escape hatch" I have made the code so that it will use chardet
    first if it is installed, but we no longer depend upon it directly,
    although there is a new extra added, `requests[lgpl]`. This should
    minimize the impact to users, and give them an escape hatch if
    charset_normalizer turns out to be not as good. (In my non-exhaustive
    tests it detects the same encoding as chartdet in every case I threw at
    it)

part.text:
The `requests` library transitioned its default text-encoding detector from `chardet` to `charset_normalizer` to address licensing ambiguity. The `chardet` library is licensed under the LGPL, which caused concerns for downstream users who might want to bundle `requests` (and therefore its dependencies) into their own projects without being subject to LGPL requirements. By moving to `charset_normalizer`, which is MIT-licensed, this ambiguity was removed.

This change was implemented in commit `2ed84f55b22f19a1e1e8eea2e50963dce62052d3`.

As stated in the commit message:
> "Although using the (non-vendored) chardet library is fine for requests itself, but using a LGPL dependency the story is a lot less clear for downstream projects... By changing out this dependency for one under MIT we remove all license ambiguity."

The library still maintains `chardet` as an optional dependency (accessible via an extra) for those who prefer it or require it for backwards compatibility, as noted in the commit message:
> "As an 'escape hatch' I have made the code so that it will use chardet first if it is installed, but we no longer depend upon it directly..."
